summary: Inspect authored seams, island distortion, relative texel density and the actual runtime UV set or transform with a diagnostic texture that leaves production maps untouched.
objective: A stretched, discontinuous or blurry region can be traced to a named mesh, UV set, island, texture role and transform rather than judged from a beauty render alone.
applies_when: Texture scale, seams, padding or coordinates differ across parts or after glTF delivery.
intent_signals: wrong UV set on one material
example_prompts: Overlay a checker and identify UV islands whose scale differs from adjacent panels.
Inspect which TEXCOORD set and transform each loaded material texture actually uses.
negative_signals: one texel density for every asset
judge UVs from base color only
not_for: Choosing a universal texture resolution budget.
Procedural 3D coordinates with no UV-dependent delivered texture.

principles: Distinguish four questions: seam placement, shape distortion, relative surface coverage and runtime coordinate selection. One checker view does not answer all four.
Texel density is a project comparison tied to texture resolution, UV coverage and modeled surface scale; prescribe consistency only where the intended material and viewing task require it.
Inspect the texture role's actual coordinate set and transform. A good active UV map in Blender does not prove a delivered base-color, normal, light or occlusion texture samples that set.
A seam is not automatically a defect. Evaluate visibility, tangent continuity, material boundary, atlas padding and intended concealment.
implementation: In Blender, show seam overlays and UV-editor Display Stretch by angle and area; apply a labeled square-and-axis checker to selected source objects without overwriting production images.

Record object scale policy, UV map name, image dimensions and intended density groups. Compare islands by an explicit surface-area-to-UV-area calculation or a checker at the approved view distance, and disclose mirrored or intentionally rescaled islands.

After load, isolate the mesh and inspect each material texture role's coordinate channel, offset, rotation, scale and sampler. Use the linked KHR_texture_transform record for extension-specific handoff.
Test seam neighborhoods with normal and color diagnostics separately, then test atlas padding under the actual minification and mip policy. Keep inspection textures and material clones disposable.
Reset restores the original materials, color-space annotations, texture transforms and texture ownership without disposing shared production textures.
observable_checks: Use one equal-density pair, one deliberately scaled hero island, one angle-stretched island and one accidental scale mismatch; the report distinguishes intention from defect.
Inspect a material whose texture selects a nondefault TEXCOORD set and transform; the runtime overlay follows the sampled coordinates rather than Blender's currently active UV map.
Orbit across a marked seam under a tangent-space normal test and shrink the object through mip levels; report tangent discontinuity and padding bleed separately.
Disable inspection and verify production textures, channel selection, transforms and shared-resource counts return to the pre-inspection state.

creative_affordances: Use numbered checker cells, density bands or synchronized UV and 3D selection.
Group hero, background and tiled surfaces by declared visual purpose rather than forcing identical density.
known_limits: No universal pixels-per-metre or acceptable stretch threshold is asserted.
Runtime texture filtering and compression can affect appearance independently of UV layout.
Authored source-checked diagnostic guidance; no UV bake, export, texture upload or render was run.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5 can display UV unwrapping seams in the 3D viewport, and its UV Editor Display Stretch overlay visualizes UV-to-3D shape distortion using angle or area modes.
claims.scope: Blender source inspection only; this does not define a texel-density target or identify a runtime material's selected UV set.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 defines TEXCOORD_n as VEC2 texture-coordinate attributes with consecutively numbered set indices starting at zero, while a texture binding may select its texture-coordinate index.
claims.scope: Core glTF coordinate attributes and texture binding; extension transforms, image resolution and sampler behavior require separate inspection.
